titre_page: How to make your own nodes with “My nodes”? | Yop2D guide
description: Group nodes into a node of your own, run it from any scene and add settings to make your own blocks in Yop2D, without code (programmers call it a “function”).
h1: How to make your own nodes (My nodes)?
carte: Group nodes into a single node of your own and reuse it everywhere, with its own settings.
etapes: Resources → My nodes → ＋, then open its Blueprint.
A start event, then the nodes you want.
The “Run one of my nodes” node in a scene.
A name, a type, a starting value.
blocs: **A node of your own** is a small group of nodes that you give a name to (programmers call it a “function”). You build it once, then run it whenever you want with a single node, from any scene. It is your way of making **your own blocks**: you don't redo the same thing ten times and your Blueprints stay tidy.
a project open in the editor.
Open the **Resources** panel (on the left of the editor) and unfold the **My nodes** part.
Tap **＋**, type a short name (for example `Give_points`) and confirm.
Tap your node's name to select it, then the button that opens its Blueprint (the icon of linked nodes).
Your node is a file of your project: it is exported with your game and works in every scene.
You are in your node's Blueprint (the title says “My node: …”). Place the [[NoeudEventStart]] event: this is where your node starts.
Then connect the nodes you want. For this example: [[ajouter_variable]] (variable `score`), then [[toast]].
In a scene's Blueprint, add the [[appeler_fonction]] node.
Tap the choice line and pick your node.
When this node is reached, the nodes you put inside run, then the Blueprint carries on.
Be careful not to put [[appeler_fonction]] under [[NoeudEventChaqueImage]] by accident: your node would start again on every frame.
Without settings, your node always does the same thing. **Settings** let you adjust it each time: how many points, which message, what speed…
In your node's Blueprint, tap the **My node settings** button (a sliders icon, in the top bar).
Tap **+ Add an input**. Give it a **name** (for example `points`), a **type** (Number, Text or Yes / no) and a **starting value** (for example 10). Confirm, then save with 💾.

Inside your node, use the setting by writing `=points` in place of a number. For example, put `=points` in the value of [[ajouter_variable]]. For a message, put `=message` in the text setting of [[toast]].
Go back to the scene's Blueprint: the [[appeler_fonction]] node now shows one line per setting. Change the value: 50 points here, 10 points elsewhere.

A setting can also receive a calculation, for example `=score * 2`. If you leave the line as it is, the starting value is used. Inside your node, a setting takes priority over a variable with the same name.
**“Node not found”:** it was renamed or deleted. Choose it again in [[appeler_fonction]].
**Nothing happens:** check that there is a [[NoeudEventStart]] event at the start of your node, and that you saved with 💾.
**The setting lines don't appear:** save your node with its settings first, then reopen the [[appeler_fonction]] node.
**A setting name is refused:** write it as one word (letters, digits and _), without spaces.
**A node that runs itself:** Yop2D stops after a few calls so the game doesn't freeze.
